blocks.text: After your Sandbox subscription is enabled, your organization's sandbox API tokens are initially provisioned by Zscaler, enabled, and displayed within the Sandbox API Token page along with the base URL. An organization can only have one API token for the Sandbox Submission API. To learn more, see Getting Started.
From the Sandbox API Token page, you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add a new API token.
Your organization can only have 5 API tokens. If you have the maximum amount created, you must delete an existing token before you can add a new one.
Be aware that regenerating the token immediately invalidates the previous token used in any previous configurations.
To add a new cloud service API token:
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API.
Select the Sandbox API Token tab.
If you already have 5 tokens on the Sandbox API Token tab, make sure that you delete an existing token. After a token is removed, the Add Sandbox API Token option becomes available.
Click Add Sandbox API Token.
See image.
The new API token is displayed on the tab. Enter a name and click Save. You can then view the Sandbox API Token (hidden by default) by clicking the View icon.
Regenerate the API token.
This action cannot be undone.
To regenerate the Sandbox API token:
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API.
On the Sandbox API Token tab, click the Regenerate icon.
The Regenerate API Token window appears.
In the Regenerate API Token window, click Regenerate API Token.
See image.
After this, a randomized token string is immediately generated and the old string is invalidated.
Delete the API token.
This action cannot be undone.
To delete the Sandbox API token:
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API.
On the Sandbox API Token tab, click the Delete icon.
The Delete API Token window appears.
In the Delete API Token window, manually enter CONFIRM in the field provided and click Delete.
See image.
After this, the token is immediately removed and invalidated.

blocks.text: Your Sandbox API token can be disabled by Zscaler or your service provider. The token might be disabled if your organization exceeds the threshold number of API calls allowed or the code developed for your organization violates Zscaler's terms and conditions. If this occurs, the ability to add, regenerate, or delete the token is removed and a Disabled status appears. You must contact Zscaler Support or your service provider to re-enable the token.

If your Sandbox subscription expires, you still have access to the Sandbox API Token page, but you cannot make any modifications (i.e., you lose access to the POST and PUT actions within the API). Also, your existing API token is still valid but disabled. If this occurs, contact Zscaler Support. The API token is re-enabled after your subscription is renewed.
